directions.label: Practical Tips
directions.guidance: One concrete filming technique, usable today, phone or camera. Say where to try it and what to watch for while filming.

subjects.label: Stable footage
subjects.guidance: Two-handed phone technique, bracing against walls, micro-movements that read as shake, and when a tripod genuinely helps.

subjects.label: Shooting for the edit
subjects.guidance: Capturing variety on purpose: wide, medium, close; clean cutaway material; head and tail handles on every clip.

subjects.label: Audio comes first
subjects.guidance: Why viewers forgive soft video but not bad sound; room tone, mic placement, and recording a safety track.

subjects.label: Lighting for video
subjects.guidance: Window-as-key-light setups, avoiding mixed colour temperatures, and keeping exposure consistent across a shot.

directions.label: Common Mistakes
directions.guidance: A real mistake first-time shooters make, why it costs them, and the fix. Respectful tone — the mistake should feel obvious only in hindsight.

subjects.label: Zooming mid-shot
subjects.guidance: Digital zoom degrading quality, nervous zoom movement, and the cleaner habit of moving your feet or cutting between fixed frames.

subjects.label: Ignoring the background
subjects.guidance: Distracting movement, clutter and people walking through frame; why video backgrounds are alive and need more control than photos.

subjects.label: Filming the wrong shape
subjects.guidance: Shooting landscape for a vertical-first platform or vice versa; deciding the destination before pressing record.

subjects.label: Clips that are too short
subjects.guidance: Stopping record too early — the last second is where the cut needs room; holding three extra seconds is free insurance.

directions.label: Mini Lessons
directions.guidance: Explain one video concept clearly in under 60 words: name it, show how it works, give one way to practise it.

subjects.label: Frame rates
subjects.guidance: Why 24 feels cinematic, why 60 looks smooth, and how slow motion is created in-camera rather than in the edit.

subjects.label: Shot coverage
subjects.guidance: The wide-medium-close system: what each shot buys the editor and why a scene without coverage cannot be cut.

subjects.label: Movement with purpose
subjects.guidance: Every camera move should reveal or follow something; decorative movement draws attention to itself.

directions.label: For Your Business
directions.guidance: Connect video craft to a business outcome: clarity for customers, trust through faces and voices, reuse of footage across platforms. Never pitch; teach the principle.

subjects.label: Explainer videos
subjects.guidance: How a 60-second explanation of what you do beats a paragraph of copy; structuring problem → solution → next step.

subjects.label: Footage reuse
subjects.guidance: Planning one shoot to feed months of content: capturing extra frames, alternate angles, and vertical versions on the day.

subjects.label: Testimonial filming
subjects.guidance: Why clients relax off-camera, how question order builds a natural answer, and why authenticity beats scripting.

directions.label: Let's Talk Video
directions.guidance: A light, answerable question about video habits. Make it feel like the start of a conversation at a studio, not a poll.

subjects.label: Videos worth rewatching
subjects.guidance: Questions about which videos people replay and what makes the second viewing worthwhile.

subjects.label: Storytelling on phone
subjects.guidance: How people already tell stories with their phones daily, and what one small upgrade changes most.
